svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Haemodialysis: a machine that does the work of failed kidneys."], [1, "Blood is pumped from the patient\u2019s arm through the dialyser."], [3.5, "Dialysis fluid flows the other way, outside partially permeable tubing."], [6, "Urea and excess ions diffuse out of the blood, down their concentration gradients."], [9.5, "Glucose is not lost: the fluid has the same glucose concentration. Cells and proteins are too big to pass."], [12.5, "Clean blood returns to a vein."]]
svg.title: Haemodialysis
svg.desc: A haemodialysis machine: blood from the arm is pumped through partially permeable tubing with countercurrent dialysis fluid; urea and excess ions diffuse out, glucose, proteins and cells stay, and blood returns to a vein.
svg.text: Simplified. The dialyser is shown magnified as one tube.

g.data-info: Blood is taken from a vein in the arm that has been joined to an artery (a fistula), then pumped through the machine. Heparin prevents clotting.
After a bubble trap removes air. A session takes about 4 hours, three times a week.

Contains glucose and ions at the same concentrations as normal blood plasma and no urea. It flows in the opposite direction to the blood (countercurrent) to keep a concentration gradient all along the membrane.
Thin tubing with tiny pores: small molecules (urea, ions, water, glucose) can pass; blood cells and proteins are too large.

g.data-name: Urea and excess ions diffuse out
g.data-info: Down their concentration gradient into the dialysis fluid, which is constantly replaced.
g.aria-label: Urea and excess ions diffuse out

g.text: urea and excess ions diffuse out

g.data-info: There is no glucose gradient (same concentration on both sides), and proteins and cells are too large to cross.

g.text: glucose (green): same on both sides · proteins (purple) too large
• glucose at the normal blood concentration
